hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image across the roadway

hazards.name: Wide multi-lane roadway
hazards.description: Four lanes of traffic without a median or refuge increases exposure time and risk for pedestrians crossing mid-block.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the image, spanning the width of the road.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked cars
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb can block the line of sight between drivers and pedestrians entering the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image along the far curb where the silver car and pickup truck are parked.

hazards.name: Visual Obstructions from Parking
hazards.description: Parked vehicles along the curb block sightlines between pedestrians on the sidewalk and drivers in the travel lanes.

hazards.name: Lack of marked crossings
hazards.description: No designated crossing points are visible in this mid-block section, which may encourage unsafe crossings.

hazards.name: Open vehicle trunk obstruction
hazards.description: A parked vehicle has its trunk open, extending into the sidewalk area and creating a physical obstacle for pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Foreground, left side of the image near the blue car.

hazards.name: Reduced natural surveillance
hazards.description: Closed metal shutters on all visible storefronts eliminate 'eyes on the street', which can decrease the perceived and actual safety of pedestrians.

hazards.name: Excessive Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross at least four lanes of traffic, increasing exposure time to vehicles.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Infrastructure
hazards.description: The large utility pole located on the refuge island may obstruct a driver's view of a pedestrian waiting to cross.

hazards.name: Unsignalized Multi-lane Crossing
hazards.description: Crossing multiple lanes of traffic without a pedestrian signal or traffic light creates high-conflict potential.

hazards.name: Lack of Buffer
hazards.description: Pedestrians on the sidewalk are directly adjacent to moving traffic with no physical separation.
hazards.location_in_image: Curb line on both sides of the street

hazards.name: Blank Frontage
hazards.description: Shuttered storefronts and a fenced vacant lot reduce natural surveillance and can make the environment feel less safe for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Lack of Mid-block Crossing
hazards.description: There are no marked crossing points visible in the immediate vicinity, which may lead to unsafe mid-block crossings.

hazards.name: High-speed roadway design
hazards.description: The wide, multi-lane roadway with clear sightlines and lack of traffic calming encourages higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Metal Grates
hazards.description: Large metal utility grates integrated into the sidewalk can be slippery when wet and may have uneven edges.

hazards.name: Temporary Fencing
hazards.description: Chain-link fencing and a traffic barrel obstruct a portion of the sidewalk area under the marquee.
hazards.location_in_image: Sidewalk area under the building marquee

hazards.name: Wide Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The four-lane roadway width creates a long, unprotected crossing distance for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Wide, straight travel lanes
hazards.description: The wide and straight geometry of the travel lanes may encourage vehicle speeds that are unsafe for an urban pedestrian context.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: Temporary construction fencing and debris on the left side of the image restrict the usable width of the sidewalk.

hazards.name: Parked cars near intersection
hazards.description: Parked vehicles close to the crosswalk can obstruct sightlines between drivers and pedestrians at the intersection.

hazards.name: Sightline obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles near the crosswalk may obscure pedestrians from oncoming drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the image where the blue car is parked

hazards.name: Sightline Obstructions
hazards.description: Parked vehicles, particularly the large truck on the right, can obscure pedestrians from the view of oncoming drivers.

hazards.name: Poor Roadway Pavement
hazards.description: The asphalt surface shows signs of wear and cracking, which can create tripping hazards if pedestrians cross mid-block.
hazards.location_in_image: Center foreground, across the roadway surface.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at potential crossing points to increase pedestrian visibility and reduce crossing distance.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Add marked crosswalks with high-visibility paint to designate safe crossing locations.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming Measures
interventions.description: Implement speed humps or chicanes to reduce vehicle speeds on this straight corridor.

interventions.title: Midblock Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk
interventions.description: Mark a midblock crossing with high-visibility paint and appropriate signage.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Furniture Zone
interventions.description: Add a buffer of street trees or planters between the sidewalk and the roadway to improve comfort and safety.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Repair and Infill
interventions.description: Pave the missing section of the sidewalk to restore a continuous, level, and ADA-compliant walking surface.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Buffer Zone
interventions.description: Install street trees or planters in the furniture zone to provide a physical buffer between pedestrians and moving traffic.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Mid-block Crossing
interventions.description: Add a marked crosswalk with high-visibility paint and signage to provide a legal and safer place for pedestrians to cross this long block.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking near potential crossing points or intersections to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Mid-block Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane at potential crossing points to shorten crossing distance and improve visibility.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a raised median or refuge island to provide a safe mid-point for pedestrians crossing the wide roadway.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Landscaping
interventions.description: Add a buffer zone with street trees to provide physical separation and improve the pedestrian experience.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Planters
interventions.description: Install street trees or large planters to provide a physical and psychological buffer between the wide sidewalk and the roadway.

interventions.title: Mid-block Crosswalk
interventions.description: Add a high-visibility marked crosswalk, potentially with a Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacon (RRFB), to provide a safe crossing point.

interventions.title: Road Diet
interventions.description: Reduce the number of travel lanes to include bike lanes or a center turn lane, narrowing the crossing distance for pedestrians.

interventions.title: Lane Narrowing or Road Diet
interventions.description: Reduce the width or number of travel lanes to slow traffic and repurpose space for bike lanes or wider buffers.

interventions.title: Active Frontage Incentives
interventions.description: Encourage the use of transparent security grilles instead of solid shutters to maintain visibility and engagement with the street after hours.

interventions.title: Mid-block Crossing
interventions.description: Install a marked mid-block crosswalk with high-visibility markings and signage.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Replace standard parallel line markings with continental or zebra patterns to increase visibility to approaching drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon (HAWK)
interventions.description: Install a signalized crossing to provide a protected interval for pedestrians to cross this wide arterial.

interventions.title: Street Furniture and Planters
interventions.description: Install benches and large planters along the curb to provide a physical and psychological buffer from traffic and activate the wide sidewalk.

interventions.title: Pedestrian-Scale Lighting
interventions.description: Add street lamps to improve visibility and safety, particularly near the transit entrance and along the blank walls.

interventions.title: Protected Bike Lanes
interventions.description: Repurpose a portion of the wide roadway for protected bike lanes to provide a buffer between pedestrians and moving traffic.

interventions.title: Mid-block Crossing with Refuge Island
interventions.description: Install a marked crosswalk with a raised median refuge to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Buffer
interventions.description: Install street furniture, planters, or bollards to provide physical separation between the wide sidewalk and the roadway.

interventions.title: Frontage Activation
interventions.description: Encourage the restoration and active use of the building's ground floor to improve natural surveillance and pedestrian comfort.

interventions.title: Surface Uniformity
interventions.description: Ensure all sidewalk grates are slip-resistant and perfectly flush with the surrounding pavement to prevent trips and slips.

interventions.title: Street trees and buffers
interventions.description: Add a line of street trees or a furniture zone to provide a physical and psychological buffer between the sidewalk and the roadway.

interventions.title: Traffic Calming
interventions.description: Introduce speed humps or cushions to reduce vehicle speeds along this straight stretch.
